Independent answers: 8 yes, age 18, country residence 2 years and local residence 8 months pass; 9 first person only, since 8 months exceeds 6 and 3 months falls short; 10 neither reading test nor land ownership may be required; 11 safeguard ballot secrecy and sanctity, legislate overseas voting, and design independent voting for disabled/illiterate voters with interim legal and COMELEC safeguards. findings.problem: The citizenship flow does not give a branch for a person in the pre-1973 group who has not validly elected citizenship. Its yes branch goes straight to valid election and natural-born status. It also leaves the citizen-at-adoption route without an outcome. An artist cannot draw a complete decision flow from these instructions without supplying legal decisions.

checked: Citizenship is defined first. Election is distinguished from voting; majority is explained with the general current age and a historical-law caution. Natural-born and naturalization are defined before example use.

Alien is explained within the naturalization paragraph; oath of allegiance, certificate of candidacy, repatriation, dual citizenship, dual allegiance and suffrage receive local explanations. Age and residence units are ordinary years and months. No prerequisite teaching is needed to follow the examples.
The lesson explains citizenship through the four legal routes and birth-parent timing, then explains natural-born status and the election exception through their legal effects.

Marriage, reacquisition by oath, separate candidacy renunciation and dual status are explained as distinct processes or conditions. Voting is taught through minimum qualifications, registration, legal disqualification and ballot protections. These explanations support all worked cases.
The text limits the election route to pre-January 17, 1973 births, checks parent citizenship at birth, separates birthplace from citizenship and limits the marriage rule by legal renunciation.

Naturalization residence is described as ordinary, with the Section 3 reduction and separate RA 9139 process; other qualifications and barriers are acknowledged. RA 9225 is limited to natural-born Filipinos naturalized abroad and distinguishes reacquisition from candidacy.

Voting conditions include election-day age and residence, registration and statutory barriers. The lesson rejects reading/property tests and explains overseas voting conditions and the interim arrangement pending independent voting procedures.
